The answer 30 matches my recollection of the known result, but I did not verify it independently. The proposed solution's own argument is also not rigorous.

**What the solution gets right.** It reduces to computing the top cohomology of Γ_{0,3}^+(p) (degree 3) via the Steinberg module. It finds vanishing for p = 2, 3, 5, 7, 13 and non-vanishing for p = 11, 17, 19. It also notes that the genus of X_0(p) is zero exactly for p ∈ {2, 3, 5, 7, 13}, which gives the set {2, 3, 5, 7, 13}. As I recall, the published theorem says the top cohomology for n = 3 vanishes exactly for p = 2, 3, 5, 7, 13.

**Where the solution is weak.** The step "the boundary system is exactly weight-2 modular symbols of dimension g(X_0(p))" is asserted without proof. The n = 2 analogue has an Eisenstein contribution, so the match with genus is not automatic. The explicit case checks are only sketched.

The sum is 2 + 3 + 5 + 7 + 13 = 30.

VERDICT: ACCEPT
